No spam - genuine quotes from vetted UK engine specialists only. 8,000+ Engine Codes 40+ Car Brands 100% Free · No Obligation Make Select Make Series Model Select a model Year Select Model First Engine Code Get Free Engine Quotes At a glance · what your coolant warning light means Match the light type to the likely cause Red thermometer Engine overheating - STOP DRIVING Critical See Overheating page Yellow/red waves Low coolant level - check soon Medium £5-£700 Red thermometer + steam Serious overheating - STOP Critical £550-£10,000+ Yellow coolant light + leak Coolant leak Medium £50-£700 Coolant light + white smoke Head gasket failure High £550-£2,000+ What this usually means in UK cars Your engine's temperature warning system The coolant warning light is your engine's temperature warning system. Unlike the red oil light (which means immediate danger), the coolant light can mean anything from a minor top-up to catastrophic overheating - depending on which light you see. In our 24,650 quote dataset, we identified four primary causes: Low coolant level - 50% of cases Simple top-up required. Cost: £5-£150. Coolant leak - 30% of cases External leak from hose, radiator, or water pump. Cost: £50-£700. Thermostat failure - 12% of cases Stuck closed, causing overheating. Cost: £80-£300. Head gasket failure - 8% of cases Coolant entering combustion chamber. Cost: £550-£2,000+. The critical distinction: 🔴 Red thermometer Engine overheating STOP DRIVING IMMEDIATELY 🟡 Yellow/red waves Low coolant level Check when cool, top up Light types - what each one means Know which light you're seeing 🌡️ RED Thermometer Static Engine overheating STOP DRIVING 〰️ YELLOW/RED Waves Static Low coolant level Check when cool 🌡️ RED Thermometer Flashing Rapid overheating STOP DRIVING 🌡️ RED Thermometer With beep Critical overheating STOP DRIVING 〰️ YELLOW/RED Waves Flashing Very low coolant Check immediately Common affected vehicles & engines Coolant warning light issues by make and model Vehicle Common Engine Code Typical Coolant Light Issue Cost Range BMW 3-Series (E90) N47 2.0d Water pump failure (electric) £400-£700 BMW 5-Series (F10) N57 3.0d Thermostat housing £300-£500 VW Golf / Audi A3 EA189 2.0 TDI EGR cooler failure £400-£800 VW Golf / Audi A3 EA888 2.0 TSI Water pump failure £300-£600 Ford Focus / Mondeo 1.6/2.0 TDCi Radiator leak £300-£600 Ford Fiesta 1.0 EcoBoost Head gasket (known issue) £600-£1,500 Vauxhall Astra 1.6/2.0 CDTi Water pump £300-£500 Mercedes C-Class OM651 2.1d Thermostat housing £200-£500 Audi A4 / A6 EA288 2.0 TDI EGR cooler failure £400-£800 Mini Cooper N14/N18 1.6 Water pump/thermostat housing £300-£600 Jaguar XF / XJ 2.2/3.0d Thermostat housing £400-£700 Renault Mégane 1.5/2.0 dCi Thermostat failure £200-£400 What people think vs reality The expensive mistake is ignoring the light “The light came on but the gauge is fine - I'll keep driving.” The coolant light is a warning. The gauge is the confirmation. Don't ignore the light. “I'll just top up the coolant when I get home.” Coolant loss while driving can lead to rapid overheating. Stop and check. “Opening the coolant reservoir is fine when hot.” NEVER open the coolant reservoir when hot. Pressurised coolant causes severe burns. “I'll just use water - it's fine.” Water isn't coolant. It boils at a lower temperature and lacks corrosion inhibitors. Use proper coolant. “The light came on once and went off - it's fine.” Intermittent lights indicate intermittent problems. The fault is still there. Diagnostic flowchart Follow this decision tree to identify the cause COOLANT WARNING LIGHT │ ├─── Which light is on? │ │ │ ├── RED thermometer → STOP ENGINE → Emergency │ │ │ └── YELLOW waves (coolant level) → Check coolant (cold) │ ├─── Check coolant level (engine COLD) │ │ │ ├── Normal → Sensor or wiring → Coolant sensor │ │ │ └── Low → Top up and monitor → Coolant leak │ ├─── Any other symptoms? │ │ │ ├── White smoke → Head gasket → Head gasket │ │ │ ├── Puddle under car → External leak → Coolant leak │ │ │ ├── Heater not working → Air in system → Air lock │ │ │ └── No other symptoms → Monitor │ └─── Professional diagnostic (£50-£150) │ ├── Pressure test → Find external leaks │ ├── Exhaust gas test → Check for head gasket │ └── Thermostat check → Check if stuck Coolant warning light types & repair costs Use the light type to understand the repair range Symptom Pattern What It Means Typical Repair Cost Range YELLOW coolant light + normal level Sensor or wiring fault Sensor replacement £50-£150 YELLOW coolant light + low level Low coolant - top-up needed Coolant top-up £5-£150 YELLOW coolant light + frequent top-ups Coolant leak Leak repair £50-£700 RED thermometer + temperature gauge high Overheating STOP DRIVING - diagnostic £80-£10,000+ RED thermometer + steam Serious overheating STOP DRIVING - diagnostic £550-£10,000+ Coolant light + white smoke Head gasket failure Head gasket replacement £550-£2,000+ Coolant light + puddle under car External leak Component replacement £50-£800 Coolant light + heater not working Air in system System bleed £50-£150 Coolant light + fan not working Fan failure Fan replacement £100-£300 ⚠️ Red thermometer = stop driving immediately If the red thermometer light comes on: Pull over safely - Find a safe location immediately Turn off engine - Do not wait. Turn off the key immediately Wait 30+ minutes - Do not open the bonnet. Coolant is pressurised Do not add coolant - Wait for the engine to cool completely Call for recovery - Do not drive Why this is critical: The red thermometer means the engine is overheating Overheating causes cylinder head warping, head gasket failure, and piston seizure Continuing to drive will destroy the engine Check when cool: Never open the coolant reservoir when the engine is hot Pressurised coolant can spray out and cause severe burns Wait at least 30 minutes before checking 🟡 Yellow coolant light (waves) = Check when cool The yellow waves light means low coolant level. Check the level when the engine is cold. Top up to the correct level. Monitor for future loss (indicates a leak). Book Emergency Recovery + Diagnostic What happens if you ignore it - detailed progression From £5 to £10,000+ Stage What Happens Cost 1. Coolant light (yellow) Low coolant level - top-up needed £5-£150 2. Coolant light (yellow) + frequent top-ups Leak in system £50-£700 3. Leak ignored Coolant level drops, overheating begins £50-£700 4. Overheating (brief) Head gasket fails £550-£2,000 5. Overheating (prolonged) Cylinder head warps £1,000-£3,000 6. Engine seizure Block cracks, engine destroyed £2,500-£10,000+ The £5,000+ mistake: “I'll just top up the coolant and keep driving.” A £50-£700 leak repair becomes a £2,500-£10,000+ engine replacement. What to do next Identify, check, diagnose Step 1: Identify which light is on Red thermometer? → STOP DRIVING Yellow/red waves? → Check coolant level (when cold) Step 2: Check coolant level (when cold) Wait 30+ minutes after driving · Open the coolant reservoir slowly (cover with a cloth) · Is the level between min and max? Step 3: If coolant level is low Top up to the correct level · Use the correct coolant type for your vehicle · Monitor for future loss Step 4: If coolant level drops again Book a diagnostic (£50-£150) - there is a leak in the system Step 5: Professional diagnostic (£50-£150) A technician will pressure test the cooling system, check for exhaust gases in coolant (head gasket test), inspect for external leaks, and test thermostat and water pump function. Engine overheating. Stop driving immediately. What does the yellow coolant wave light mean? Low coolant level. Check the level when the engine is cold. Can I open the coolant reservoir when the engine is hot? No. Pressurised coolant can spray out and cause severe burns. Wait 30+ minutes. How much does a coolant leak repair cost in the UK? Coolant leak repair costs £50-£700 depending on the cause. Hoses: £50-£200. Radiator: £300-£800. Is the coolant light the same as the temperature gauge? They are related. The coolant light is a warning. The temperature gauge shows the actual temperature. If both indicate a problem - stop immediately.

blocks.question: What does the red thermometer light mean?
What does the yellow coolant wave light mean?
blocks.answer: Low coolant level. Check the level when the engine is cold.

blocks.question: Can I open the coolant reservoir when the engine is hot?
blocks.answer: No. Pressurised coolant can spray out and cause severe burns. Wait 30+ minutes.

blocks.question: How much does a coolant leak repair cost in the UK?
blocks.answer: Coolant leak repair costs £50-£700 depending on the cause. Hoses: £50-£200. Radiator: £300-£800.

blocks.question: Is the coolant light the same as the temperature gauge?
blocks.answer: They are related. The coolant light is a warning. The temperature gauge shows the actual temperature. If both indicate a problem - stop immediately.
